headline: ABRASILVER LOCKS IN FINAL PERMITS AT C$4.2B NPV DIABLILLOS — BOTH PROVINCES CLEARED, CONSTRUCTION PREP Q3 2026 (TSX:ABRA)
source_name: Investing News Network / AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX:ABRA)
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX:ABRA) delivered a pair of knockout milestones in a single week: on June 23 the company published a Definitive Feasibility Study confirming a 25-year, 9,000 t/day open-pit operation with a C$4.2 billion after-tax NPV5% and 42% IRR at the Diablillos silver-gold project in Argentina, followed on June 24 by receipt of the Environmental Impact Assessment approval from Catamarca Province — the last major provincial permit required for a construction decision. With DIA approvals now in hand from both Salta (April 27) and Catamarca (June 24), and eligibility for Argentina's RIGI investment incentive regime providing 25% corporate tax and 0% export duties, AbraSilver plans to begin early-works and site preparation in Q3 2026 — making Diablillos one of the world's most advanced large-scale undeveloped silver projects at precisely the moment the global silver supply deficit has entered its sixth consecutive year.

headline: GRANDE PORTAGE LANDS OCEAN PARTNERS: C$6M EQUITY + US$25M LOAN + 7-YEAR 100% GOLD OFFTAKE AT NEW AMALGA, ALASKA (TSXV:GPG)
source_name: Access Newswire / Grande Portage Resources Ltd. (TSXV:GPG)
snippet: Grande Portage Resources (TSXV:GPG) announced June 25 binding term sheets with Ocean Partners UK Limited covering three simultaneous components: a C$6 million equity investment at an above-market price that makes Ocean Partners the #2 shareholder behind Eric Sprott; a US$25 million construction loan and overrun facility; and a commercial offtake agreement for up to 100% of production at the New Amalga Gold Project in southeast Alaska for the first seven years of commercial operation. The deal's structural innovation eliminates the need for a processing and tailings disposal facility on-site by selling sorted ore directly to Ocean Partners, materially reducing capital, operating costs, and regulatory complexity — and clearing the capital stack for a project that is targeting all authorizations by mid-2029 and first production in 2031 under the U.S. federal NEPA environmental review process.

headline: BOLD VENTURES HITS 100.7 g/t AU OVER 2.95m — 476 g/t BONANZA CORE, TRAXXIN EAST PARALLEL ZONE OPENS UP; THUNDER BAY (TSXV:BOL)
snippet: Bold Ventures Inc. (TSXV:BOL) reported June 25 that drill hole TX-26-02 at the Traxxin Main Zone west-northwest of Thunder Bay, Ontario, returned 100.7 g/t gold over 2.95 metres — including a bonanza-grade core of 476 g/t gold over 0.6 metres — while a second hole confirmed a new east-side parallel zone of gold mineralisation not previously intersected in this orientation, indicating the Traxxin deposit is substantially wider than its current footprint. The combination of extreme near-surface high grades and the opening of a new structural corridor on the east side materially upgrades the project's scale potential and feeds into planned follow-up drilling designed to define the extent of the parallel system.

headline: SKYHARBOUR + ORANO PLAN 3,500m SUMMER DRILL AT PRESTON LAKE, ATHABASCA BASIN (TSXV:SYH)
snippet: Skyharbour Resources (TSXV:SYH) and joint venture partner Orano Canada — one of the world's largest uranium producers — announced June 23 upcoming summer 2026 exploration and diamond drilling plans at the Preston Lake Uranium Project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, targeting 3,500 metres across multiple geophysical conductors in the basin that hosts the world's highest-grade uranium deposits. Orano's active earn-in at Preston Lake provides institutional geological support and differentiates Skyharbour's asset from self-funded juniors in the district, while uranium spot prices near $85–87/lb sustain the economics that have driven a new Athabasca exploration cycle across the basin in 2025–2026.

headline: HAMILTON: GOLD SUMMER DOLDRUMS '26 NEAR END — AUTUMN RALLY LOADING FROM MID-JULY; SEASONAL BUY SIGNAL BUILDING (GOLDSEEK)
snippet: Adam Hamilton's annual seasonal analysis of gold's summer doldrums argues that 2026's June–July weakness fits the pattern observed since 2001: gold's weakest seasonal window is compressed into June and early July, with the autumn rally historically beginning by mid-July as speculative positioning clears and physical buying from Asian and European markets picks up ahead of the September–November peak season. Hamilton's view is that the current correction — driven by FOMC hawkishness and the withdrawal of speculative longs from the $5,589 January all-time high — is indistinguishable from prior seasonal lows that preceded the largest percentage gains in the cycle, and that the mid-July inflection point is the strategic entry window for investors who have been waiting for a pullback.

headline: PENTO: FED ABOUT TO SURPRISE MARKETS — RATE CUTS COMING SOONER THAN WALL STREET BELIEVES; GOLD'S REAL MOVE HASN'T STARTED (MONEY METALS)
snippet: Michael Pento — whose call for a 2025 Fed pivot came several months ahead of consensus — argued in a June 26 Money Metals audio briefing that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is misjudging the underlying economy: the same credit contraction, delinquency acceleration, and goods-price deflation that historically precede emergency policy reversal are now visibly in place, yet CME FedWatch is pricing 90% odds of a rate hike before year-end. Pento's counter is that the first credible sign of economic cracking — likely showing up in the July NFP or Q3 earnings season — will force a pivot faster than the bond market expects, and that gold's 28% decline from the January $5,589 all-time high represents the last discounted entry point before the monetary regime shift that drives the next leg of the bull market.

headline: GOLDSEEK: SILVER'S GREAT SUMMER — DEFICIT YEAR SIX, CHINA'S STRATEGIC RECLASSIFICATION AND SOLAR DEMAND ALL POINT HIGHER
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis framing silver's current pullback from January's $121/oz all-time high as a temporary interruption of structural bull conditions argues that three converging drivers make the summer setup compelling: the Silver Institute projects a 46.3-million-ounce global supply deficit for 2026 — the sixth consecutive year of structural shortfall — while industrial demand from solar panels, EV batteries, and AI data centre cooling continues expanding; and China's January 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material places it under the same priority framework as rare earths for the first time in the metal's modern history. The analysis frames the compressed gold-silver ratio and cleared speculative positioning following the FOMC-driven selloff as conditions that have historically preceded silver's most violent recovery rallies.

headline: GLENSTAR DEPLOYS SHEAR-WAVE SEISMIC AT GREEN MONSTER NEVADA — 2,400-FT ARRAYS TO IMAGE FAULTS AND COVER AHEAD OF DRILL PHASE
snippet: Glenstar Minerals Inc. announced it will conduct a Terēan shear-wave seismic survey at its Green Monster polymetallic project in Clark County, Nevada, commencing June 29, 2026 — the first such geophysical imaging campaign at the property following a successful Phase 2 drill program completed in February 2026. The survey will deploy 2,400-foot linear arrays across four cross-sections to image cover thickness, depth to bedrock, fault structures, and voids to depths of 600 feet, providing the geological framework required to optimally site the next generation of drill holes in what the company has described as a 'geologically complex' system with high-grade polymetallic mineralisation confirmed in prior drilling. The Nevada jurisdiction benefits from incoming Section 232 copper tariff dynamics that are expected to create a domestic price premium for any copper-bearing discovery in U.S. soil.

headline: JAGUAR MINING CONFIRMS PILAR GOLD MINE BA ZONE GOES DEEPER — DOWN-PLUNGE CONTINUITY PROVEN, ADDS MINE LIFE AT $4K GOLD (TSX:JAG)
snippet: Jaguar Mining Inc. (TSX:JAG) reported results from its ongoing diamond drilling program at the Pilar Gold Mine in Minas Gerais, Brazil, demonstrating that high-grade mineralisation in the BA Zone remains robust and predictably continuous at depth — establishing down-plunge continuity along strike that supports resource expansion and incremental mine life additions at a producing asset already generating meaningful cash flow at current gold prices near $4,063/oz. The BA Zone continuity result is significant for investors evaluating Jaguar's reserve replacement trajectory at a mine that has operated since 2011, as the ability to convert exploration intercepts into reserves at an operating mine carries substantially lower permitting and infrastructure risk than greenfield discoveries.
